topic: Suitable scales, site plans, preliminary drawings, working drawings

questions.q: 52. The drawing for municipality is done at scale
questions.explain: Municipal drawings often use 1:100 (metric) or 1" = 8' (FPS) as standard scales for site plans and building layouts to ensure clarity for legal approvals.

questions.q: 53. To measure a fraction we use
questions.explain: A diagonal scale is used to represent three consecutive units (e.g., meters, decimeters, and centimeters) and can measure very small fractions of a unit.

questions.q: 54. Find the RF for scale 1cm = 25 km
questions.explain: RF = Drawing Distance / Actual Distance. 1 cm / (25 × 1000 × 100) cm = 1 / 2,500,000.

questions.q: 108. Concept drawing is normally provided for the work of
questions.explain: Concept drawings are preliminary sketches used during the tendering or bidding phase to illustrate the general idea of a project.

questions.q: 109. As built drawing is normally constructed.............the construction.
questions.explain: As-built drawings are revised sets of drawings submitted after a project is finished to reflect all changes made during construction.

questions.q: 115. The main purpose of as built drawing is
questions.explain: As-built drawings show the exact location of buried pipes or wiring, making them vital for future maintenance and repairs.

questions.q: 127. For drawing of small objects, the scale used is
questions.explain: Small objects like watch parts are drawn using an enlarged scale (e.g., 5:1) so that details are visible.

questions.q: 130. Working drawing is prepared not for
questions.explain: Specifications are written documents describing quality and materials; working drawings focus on geometry and layout.

questions.q: 131. The set of technical drawings used during the manufacturing phase of product including civil construction, are known as
questions.explain: Working drawings provide all necessary dimensions and details required to actually manufacture or build the project.

questions.q: 141. The proportion by which the actual size of an object is enlarged or reduced in drawing is simply known as
questions.explain: Scale is the ratio of the drawing size to the real-world size.

questions.q: 174. Which of the following regarding scales in drawing is NOT true?
options: the name of the scale (e.g. scale 1:10) should be mentioned below the scale
a diagonal scale consists of a primary scale and a venirer
comparative scales may be plain or diagonal
when an unusual scale is used it is constructed on the drawing sheet
questions.explain: A diagonal scale is used to read three dimensions (e.g., meters, decimeters, centimeters) but does not technically use a 'vernier' like a vernier scale does.
A site plan is an architectural document that shows the footprint of a building and its relationship to the property lines.

options: must provide complete information to produce the object
should be supplemented by further details
questions.explain: A working drawing must contain all necessary dimensions, notes, and views for a manufacturer to build the part without further questions.

questions.q: 180. *The space covered by a drawing in a paper after changing the scale from 1:100 to 1:50 will:
questions.explain: Moving from 1:100 to 1:50 makes the drawing twice as large in linear dimensions, meaning it covers four times (400%) the area. Note: the answer key marks 'd', which likely refers to a specific scale factor calculation in the textbook's context.
